notes: The rig is three stacked Analogue Systems wooden cabinets: a 1-row, a second 1-row and a 4-row cabinet. I counted them top to bottom as rows 0-5. If a corpus case must be a single case, the owner has to decide whether to keep all three. Row capacity sources. Row 0 is 168 HP: the maker's archived module list (analoguesystems.co.uk/previous_site/modules.htm) says Integrator rows are 84 HP except the 8500 series and the double sequencer cabinets, which are 168 HP, and this cabinet holds two RS-200 sequencers. Rows 2-5 are 168 HP: the maker's RS-8000 page (analoguesystems.co.uk/index.php/cabinets/rs-8000) describes a 12U walnut desk cabinet with two pairs of 168 HP rows whose halves sit at different angles, which matches the 4-row cabinet. Naming these two cabinets is my reading of the photo. Row 1 is null: the maker's pages do not identify that single-row cabinet. Scaled by the maker-stated widths of its 12 panels, it spans 167.7 HP. Widths are measured from the photo. I read each seam in perspective-rectified strips: rows 0 and 1 use their own panel-area quads, and rows 2-3 and 4-5 each use one homography per two-row block, since each pair shares a panel plane and row 4's own quad left its seams tilted. Every measured width is within 0.35 HP of a whole number, and the rounded widths sum to 168 in every row with no remainder adjustment. Rounded boundaries stay within 0.6 HP of the measured seams (row 1: 0.59; rows 0 and 2-5: 0.42 or less). The leftover error is a smooth bow across each row, from lens distortion. Corners set by hand: row 3 top edge, and row 4 top-right and bottom-right. Cross-check against the maker: every photo width matches the width Analogue Systems states (current pages for RS-200, RS-100S, RS-95e and RS-60; the archived module list for the rest) and the catalog hp wherever a catalog row exists, so there are no disagreements. The closest calls are RS-290 measured 29.7 against the maker's 30, the row-1 left-end RS-120 at 11.7, and RS-375 at 48.35 against 48. The plain RS-95 has no maker width of its own; the photo gives 12. Version calls rest on the panel text and the maker's pages. RS-60 x2 stays open-set because the maker sells RS-60 and RS-60N Envelope as separate products. RS-100 and RS-95 are the owner's choice. The maker files the RS-100S as the Mk3 under its RS100 entry, and calls the RS-95e technically identical to the RS-95 apart from the ten-turn dial. Both are left open-set as placeholders, and the alternatives are catalog RS-100S (id 635) and RS-95e (id 1467). Open-set panels (21): RS-40, RS-50 x2, RS-60 x2, RS-95, RS-100, RS-130, RS-150 x2, RS-170 x5, RS-200 x2, RS-230, RS-370, RS-375, RS-450. Unrelated to the labels: several catalog module_type values for Analogue Systems look wrong. RS-85 (VC-LFO) is typed VCO, RS-20 (ring mod) is typed LFO, RS-70 and RS-420 are typed ENV, RS-380 is typed SAMP and RS-35 is typed SEQ. The Commons page has no module list (description is just "AnalogueSystems"). The right end of row 0 is slightly soft from shallow depth of field.
